subject: Acme deployment: VPC/on-prem exceptions, resourcing & timeline
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Ops <cloudops@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme deployment: VPC/on-prem exceptions, resourcing & timeline

Team and Jordan,

Following today's discovery with Acme, they confirmed they want a Private (VPC) deployment with on-prem interconnect for a subset of workloads. High-level asks from Acme:
- Dedicated VPC deployment in their AWS account with direct-connect to their on-prem colo
- An on-prem component for offline processing (air-gapped batch inference) with limited data replication
- SOC2 evidence and a few exceptions around key rotation cadence (they require HSM integration with customer-managed keys)

I've attached their ask packet and a quick network diagram. Key questions we need answered before I commit to timelines/pricing to the customer:
1) Architecture: can the current Private control plane support split-mode (hosted control plane + customer-managed on-prem inference nodes)? Any major gaps?
2) Resourcing: what level of SRE/CSA support is required to provision and operate the on-prem piece for the first 6 months?
3) Compliance: any SOC2 gaps or special evidence we need to collect for the exceptions they listed?

Attachments: acme-deployment-ask.pdf, network-diagram.vsdx

Jordan (Acme), copying your cloud ops folks — feel free to correct/append. Internal team: please reply with feasibility notes and a rough effort estimate by EOD Wednesday so I can push a draft schedule.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme deployment: VPC/on-prem exceptions, resourcing & timeline

Marcus — thanks for the summary and attaching the docs. Quick notes after a first pass:

- Product feasibility: conceptually we support a hybrid footprint (control plane in Redwood + inference nodes customer-managed), but we haven't shipped an officially supported packaged on-prem runtime for the "air-gapped batch inference" use case. That means we'll need an official distribution and onboarding runbook.
- Config surface: we need to validate the following with Eng: KMS/HSM integration patterns, KV cache persistence semantics for on-prem, and supported quantization builds for offline nodes.
- UX/ops: our Console currently assumes reachable telemetry from nodes. For air-gapped deployment we'll need an alternative log/metrics collection proposal and an ops playbook.

Can Ava and Platform weigh in with engineering constraints and a rough ETA? Jordan (legal), flagging that Acme explicitly asked about key rotation cadence — please note any contract implications.

--
Evelyn Hart
Director, Product Management — Redwood Inference

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-14T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme deployment: VPC/on-prem exceptions, resourcing & timeline

On Tue, 2026-04-12, Evelyn Hart wrote:
> Marcus — thanks for the summary and attaching the docs. Quick notes after a first pass:
>
> - Product feasibility: conceptually we support a hybrid footprint ...

I've reviewed the attachments (noted infra diagram) and did a quick scoping exercise. Summary and asks:

Technical feasibility (short answer): doable, but requires a small engineering productization effort + ops staffing.

Detailed constraints and plan:
- Control plane: can remain in Redwood (hosted). We will need a lightweight agent for the on-prem inference nodes to handle KV cache, model checksum validation, and a push-based telemetry relay for disconnected operation.
- Networking: Direct-Connect to customer VPC + static routes for the agent. Customer must provide a jump-host/egress gateway for periodic telemetry (or we operate offline batches via signed manifests).
- KMS/HSM: We can integrate with customer-managed keys using our current KMS abstraction, but HSM integration will require a small driver workstream and validation (2-3 sprints).
- Ops footprint: Recommend a minimum of 2 FTE SRE engineers from Redwood for first 3 months for onboarding, runbooks, and incident playbooks; customer to provide 1 on-prem operations contact during the same window.
- Timeline: MVP delivery (packaged runtime + onboarding playbook + basic telemetry) ~8 weeks from sign-off assuming immediate resourcing.

Risks / exceptions required:
- We'll need an SLA carveout around telemetry/alerting due to offline windows.
- We'll need an explicit exception/acknowledgement for key rotation cadence — HSM cadence may not conform to our standard managed KMS policies until the driver workstream is complete.

Attachments referenced: infra-estimate.xlsx (I dropped a rough FTE/time estimate), also added inline notes on the network diagram.

If Leadership wants to push a faster timeline, we'll need committed engineering headcount (2x eng for 8 weeks) and product owner prioritization.

— Ava Chen
Engineering Manager, Platform & Runtime

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme deployment: VPC/on-prem exceptions, resourcing & timeline

Team — quick legal/sales ops flags after reading the ask and Ava's notes:

1) Contract / procurement: Acme's HSM/KMS exception plus SLA carveouts are material. We need Sales Ops to prepare an "SLA Exception Addendum" and Legal to approve language. This will affect renewal metrics and support entitlements; recommend Finance signoff on any credits tied to those exceptions.
2) Pricing: Given the 2 FTE managed onboarding plus ongoing elevated support for 6 months, recommend a one-time onboarding fee + monthly managed-support surcharge. Marcus, please coordinate with Finance for an agreed pricing band (I suggest $40k-$70k one-time + $10k/mo surcharge as a placeholder).
3) Data residency / audit: SOC2 evidence — Acme asked for a non-standard set of artifacts in acme-soc2-exceptions.docx. Legal will review but may require an external audit supplement if they request customer-hosted log access.

I'll pick up drafting the addendum. Flagging that any SLA deviation needs an executive sign-off (VP Customer Success or above).

Jordan Blake
Head of Sales Operations (acting)

- Sales/Finance (Marcus): produce pricing proposal for onboarding + monthly managed support; propose placeholder pricing to Acme by 2026-04-20 and loop Finance if needed. (owner: marcus_lin).
- Customer (Jordan Lee / Acme Cloud Ops): confirm availability for a technical kickoff the week of 2026-04-27 and provide any missing network details or egress host info.
